title: Validation gates — how luck is removed before a strategy is trusted
description: A gate set is the difference between a leaderboard and a lottery. Hard gates cannot be overridden by profit: a strategy that made money while failing a hard gate is evidence of variance, not skill. Thresholds below are our proposed rules (a design decision), whereas every statistical method cited is from the literature register. All are implemented in engine/gates.py, which turns a bet log into this table, filled in.

columns.label: What luck or bias this removes

rows.metric: Settled bets n, and independent-game count
rows.threshold: n >= 300 bets AND >= 3 seasons OR n above the power-analysis requirement for the observed hit rate
rows.why: A 12-2 record on parlays is a coin-flip run. Power analysis (engine/stats.py) shows the sample needed to separate 55% from the 52.38% break-even is orders of magnitude larger than most claimed edges ever see, so this gate is where most strategies die — correctly.
rows.impl: stats.required_sample() and the count checks in gates.evaluate()

rows.metric: Hit rate vs break-even at the actual price paid
rows.threshold: mean hit rate > break-even(price), where break-even(-110) = 52.38%
rows.why: Removes the most common self-deception: a 'winning' record at a price whose hurdle is higher than the win rate. Break-even is computed from the price paid, not from an assumed -110.

rows.metric: mean CLV in points and in per-dollar EV vs the closing price, with a bootstrap interval
rows.threshold: median EV-vs-close > 0 and the 5% quantile of the bootstrap distribution > 0
rows.why: Profit can be luck; consistently beating the close is the closest thing to a market-based truth about whether a number is better. It also detects the 'we only win because we bet early on stale lines' case, because the benchmark is the most informative price available.
rows.impl: stats.bootstrap_ci() over per-bet CLV; requires the licensed line history (GAP-01), so until then this gate is unevaluable and no strategy can pass — stated, not worked around.

rows.metric: abstain rate and mean modelled edge per bet taken
rows.threshold: bet only when modelled EV clears break-even by the configured margin; the abstain rate must be reported with every result
rows.why: Forces the system to prove its value comes from choosing when to act, not from acting a lot. Also makes the sample-size problem visible instead of hiding it in volume.
rows.impl: policy.edge_threshold in models.json; gates.evaluate() emits the abstain rate

rows.metric: p-value of the best strategy after a Reality Check / Superior Predictive Ability correction over ALL strategies tried (including the graveyard)
rows.threshold: adjusted p < 0.05 against the no-edge benchmark
rows.why: The single most important anti-luck mechanism. With 200 candidates, five will look significant by chance at the usual cutoffs; the correction is exactly the difference between 'we found something' and 'we searched until we saw something'.
rows.impl: stats.reality_check_pvalue() — bootstrap max-T implementation of the White/Hansen idea, simplified and documented as an approximation

rows.metric: Sharpe deflated for the number of trials, parameter count and skew/kurtosis of returns
rows.threshold: deflated statistic > 0 (a positive probability of genuine skill rather than selection artefact)
rows.why: Backtest overfitting is the finance-world version of the same disease; publishing the deflated number stops a 0.9-Sharpe-in-12-lines result from being described as strong.

rows.metric: results recomputed at measured hold by market family instead of the theoretical margin
rows.threshold: must remain positive at the measured family hold; until the regulator files are parsed, use the conservative published floor for parlays rather than the singles floor
rows.why: The gap between a research result and a live one is mostly the margin you assumed. Parlays are structurally a different product — Nevada requires them to be reported separately — so they cannot inherit the singles assumption.
rows.impl: pricing.hold_adjusted_ev(); calibration data blocked at GAP-08

rows.metric: share of total PnL from one season, one team, one opponent cluster, one stadium type
rows.threshold: no single season > 45% of net PnL; no single team's games > 25%
rows.why: Isolates 'one lucky year against three bad teams' from 'a repeatable edge'. Concentration is how a model that is really about 2019 pass-scoring passes a five-year backtest.
rows.impl: gates.evaluate() splits by season, team, surface, half-of-season

rows.metric: proportion of evaluation that was out-of-sample by construction (rolling re-estimation, no peeking)
rows.threshold: 100% — a strategy score computed on any in-sample window is not a score
rows.why: Removes the largest single source of fake skill: fitting on the data you then report. It costs nothing to enforce in code and everything to enforce later.
rows.impl: engine pipeline stores fit-window and eval-window disjointness per run

rows.metric: stake limits, repricing/slippage at placement, void and push handling, promo value excluded
rows.threshold: results recomputed with limit-capped stakes and operator-legal pricing; promo-boosted EV is not counted as model skill
rows.why: Promotions are real money to a bettor and fake edge to a model. Separating them is what keeps a 'sharp' record from being a bonus-harvest record. Void and reprice handling matters most for parlays, where the house rules explicitly reprice a void leg.
rows.impl: pricing.apply_costs(); rules traced to filed house rules

rows.metric: rolling 250-bet CLV lower bound; hit-rate control chart against the fitted baseline
rows.threshold: auto-demote to research when the lower bound stays below zero across the window
rows.why: An edge that existed in 2015 and died in 2023 should not be running capital. Continuous demotion is the honest counterpart to promotion gates.
rows.impl: gates.evaluate() emits a decay flag; default rule stated in Q-22

rows.metric: market subject test against the league's prohibited classes; provenance test against the source register
rows.threshold: zero tolerance. Also: any input not present in data/sources.json fails the build
rows.why: Not about luck at all, but it outranks every performance gate: a profitable strategy that bets injury events, officiating, one-play outcomes or pre-determined roster decisions is not a strategy we may run, and one that consumes non-public information is a scandal with a spreadsheet attached.
rows.impl: engine/compliance.py, called before bet emission and in CI

rows.metric: Jaccard similarity of settled bet sets between entries; count of near-identical entries per entrant
rows.threshold: entries above 0.8 overlap are merged (or only the best-marked one is scored); maximum 5 live entries per entrant
rows.why: Without this, an entrant wins by cloning one lucky idea twenty times and picking the survivor — which is exactly the search-until-noise behaviour G-5 exists to stop, reintroduced through the leaderboard's front door.

notes: Order of operations: G-12 first (may we run it at all), then G-9 and G-3 (is the evaluation honest), then G-1, G-2, G-5, G-6 (is it distinguishable from luck), then G-7, G-8, G-10, G-4 (does it survive reality), then G-11 and G-13 (does it keep working, and is the ranking gameable).

A strategy that passes everything is still only 'not refuted'. Nothing in this gate set proves an edge; it only removes the ways a false one gets promoted. That distinction is the reason the leaderboard ranks confidence bounds rather than returns.
Where a gate is currently unevaluable (G-3 and G-7 depend on data we do not have), the correct status is 'blocked', not 'passed'. The site shows it that way.
